summary: Round 8. The round-7 major is fixed. bom.md now links the 8 arm screws to an exact Zoro M3 x 12 100-pack and the 4 VTX screws to an exact M2 x 12 20-pack. ship.py now flags any size-only price fallback on the BOM row and under the total, a test covers it, and this build has no fallback rows. The camera now runs from the stack's 9 V pad (8.99 V at the camera, rated 5-36 V), and the DESIGN.md numbers match report.json. The part geometry has not changed since round 6. Every check passes: prop gap 3.45 mm, TWR 6.18, frame 149.4 g, arm FEA 9.5 and body FEA 10.15 vs 11.67 MPa, top-plate FEA 7.03 and 8.86 vs 9.67 MPa, power 0.958 of rating, a clear cam_tilt sweep, and straight hex-key access to every screw. The open findings are all minor.

findings.issue: Carried. The generated ASSEMBLY.md step 2 says only 'Drive 8 x M3 x 12'. It never says to drop the 8 arm nuts into their top pockets, to tape or CA the 4 downward-opening stack nuts, or to use threadlocker. It also puts every soldering step after the strap. DESIGN.md has the right order, but the builder follows ASSEMBLY.md.
findings.fix: Engine: emit 'press N nuts into <part> pockets (open down: tape them)' before the step that drives their screws. Print bom_extra notes (threadlocker) at the matching step. Let the electrical steps come before a named mechanical step (here, before top_plate).

findings.issue: Carried. The BOM row says 'heat-shrink for AWG 12 joints, 20 mm pieces', but the wiring note asks for 8-10 mm at the XT60 cups, because 20 mm reaches the rear pillar. The XT60 is still held rearward only by the cable tie's friction. The hold-when-unplugging note is in WIRING.md and ASSEMBLY.md.
findings.fix: Make the AWG 12 heat-shrink row 10 mm. Optional: add a 0.8-1 mm rear retaining lip on the XT60 cradle.

findings.issue: Carried. Each arm nut sits at the bottom of an open 1 mm hex well on the phase-wire line, with the M3 x 12 tip 1 mm below the body top. Soft 18 AWG silicone pressed hard into the well could still reach the thread end. That is unlikely.
findings.fix: Optional: after torquing, put a dab of RTV or hot glue in each of the 8 wells, or a strip of Kapton under each phase bundle. Add one line to the build notes.

findings.issue: Carried. The screw tip is only about 0.3 mm past the top of the sunk nut. With the length tolerance and the tip chamfer, a short M3 x 12 engages about 1.8-2.2 mm of the 2.4 mm nut. Thread-strip strength is still well over the 144 N design load, but a nylon-insert nut cannot be used.
findings.fix: Keep the blue threadlocker on these 8 screws. In the build notes, say to check that each screw end is flush with or past the top of its nut.

findings.issue: Carried. The XT60 has no weight_g (it counts as 0 g in the mass budget), and the XING2 motor lead and CNHL pack lead gauge and length are not in the catalog. Separately, the WIRING.md loads table still uses the camera's 0.2 A draw at 5 V. At 9 V it draws about 0.08-0.1 A per the catalog note, so the table is conservative and harmless.
findings.fix: Add XT60 weight_g (about 9 g with its housing) and the lead data to the catalog, each with a source. Optional: give the camera load a per-voltage current.

findings.issue: Carried. The counterbore ceilings in the arms and the top plate open on the bed face, so each prints as a mid-air ring. This is documented in DESIGN.md only, not in the 3MF or ASSEMBLY output.
findings.fix: Turn on hole bridging / a sacrificial layer in the slicer, or model a 0.2 mm sacrificial layer. Put the note in the ASSEMBLY 'Before you start' section.

findings.issue: Carried, and handled by the documented gate. The 74 % output cap gives a central estimate of 57.4 A, and the real full-pack peak may reach about 60-66 A against the XT60's 60 A, 1-minute rating.
findings.fix: Keep the Blackbox/OSD check (peak 60 A or less) before freestyle. If the peak is over, lower motor_output_limit by 1-2 % (twr 6.18 has about 3 % margin).

findings.issue: Carried. The single strap band at x 4.5-24.5 sits 14.5 mm ahead of the pack centre, so the rear of the pack is held only by the anti-slip pad.
findings.fix: If the pack shifts in testing, add a second band at about x -36 or move the VTX back.

findings.issue: Carried. At 0 deg tilt the cheek tips, and at 35-40 deg the front corners of the roof tongue, may show at the edges of the 155 deg image. Both are clear at the 25 deg home tilt.
findings.fix: Check with the camera fitted. Chamfer or round them if they show.

findings.issue: Carried. The first arm bending mode is about 165 Hz, in the gyro noise band. The PETG-CF arm sits under a motor base that can reach 70-80 C.
findings.fix: Hover test plus a Blackbox gyro-noise check before freestyle. Consider a 0.5-1 mm standoff ring under each motor.

findings.issue: New, documentation only. The new screw:M2x12:socket price entry is a third-party Walmart listing ('Unique Bargains', 20 pcs). Its note names the right product (M2 x 12, 12.9, socket head), but neither it nor the Zoro M3 x 12 page could be opened in this review (Zoro 403, Walmart bot wall). Third-party Walmart listings tend to go stale.
findings.fix: Optional: when you next refresh prices, add a second source for M2 x 12 DIN 912 from a stable distributor (Zoro, McMaster, Accu).
